lots.guide_summary: All SOLD, all Gowans hammer prices in AUD (no conversion), Dec 2025 to Oct 2026. Ten multi-ring dress ring lots made $5 to $70, median about $23. There is no UNSOLD or ASKING evidence. The $100 bag (it also had a necklace), the single-ring, sterling silver and 9ct gold lots are left out of the range because they are not the same thing.
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD is $5 (id 411247). $5 / 1.198 = $4.17, rounded down to the nearest $5 = $0. Flip: likely resale about the $23 median. Less about 15% selling fees and about $10 postage = $9.55. $9.55 / 2.396 = $3.99, rounded down = $0. If you used the median as the keep figure instead: $23 / 1.198 = $19.20, giving $15. That is the most this lot is worth paying for as costume jewellery.
lots.confidence_reason: The identification as costume dress rings is clear and there are many Gowans SOLD results that I re-opened in the API. But no hallmarks can be read, the rings are only seen in one photo, and the 8th ring is not visible.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped from the range: 420975 ($100, a bag that also had a necklace, so not the same item). The single DRESS RING - SIZE N lots ($80 id 390066, $50 id 388509, Art Deco style $60 id 388454) are single rings, so category guide only. They are left out. QTY OF RINGS INCL STERLING SILVER and the 4/5/7 STERLING SILVER RINGS lots were not re-checked one by one and are left out. They only apply if hallmarks show silver. The 9CT GOLD ring lots ($230 to $590) are left out because nothing here is described or marked as gold. The entry for 414470 (2 DRESS RINGS, sale_price 0 with 4 bids) was mislabelled SOLD. It would belong in UNSOLD but shows no price, so I dropped it. The researcher's combined entries (several prices given as one entry) were split or dropped because one entry cannot hold several prices.
lots.key_photo_findings: One photo only. 7 rings visible, but the title says 8. The signet is gold-tone with a white enamel or mother-of-pearl style face and a raised gold emblem. That looks like modern fashion jewellery, not an antique gold signet. The blue and clear halo rings look like CZ or glass fashion rings, possibly sterling silver. No hallmarks can be read at this resolution. The shoe display is a cheap fabric novelty with a marabou feather trim.
lots.condition: Rings look bright and unworn in the photo. The display is clean. You cannot judge metal content or missing stones from the image.
lots.question_for_gowans: Are any of the 8 rings hallmarked 925, 9ct, 375 or 18k (especially the gold-tone signet and the blue-stone halo ring)? And where is the 8th ring, since only 7 show in the photo?

lots.what_it_is: Boxed toy COVERED WAGON, MADE IN ENGLAND. The box carries a diamond logo that I read as MADE BY THE P.M.C. (monogram PMC). Inside: a green wagon with a pink cloth tilt, yellow spoked wheels and shaft, and two painted metal (hollowcast or diecast) horses, one white and one tan. Probably mid 20th century English. I could not confirm which maker PMC is.
lots.guide_summary: No surviving evidence of any kind. The Gowans API has no past covered wagon lot (the only hit is this lot). WebSearch was refused because the shared budget was used up. An Invaluable keyword page returned no lot data. For context only, not a comparable: Gowans boxes of mixed old lead figures sold for $50 to $90 hammer (ids 370288 and 370286, Oct 2025; 396745, Mar 2026). That does not price this item.
lots.working: No same-item SOLD evidence, so both maximum bids are $0.
lots.confidence_reason: I read the PMC logo myself, but did not identify the maker. There is no sold, unsold or asking evidence at all.
lots.dropped_entries: The researcher gave no entries. I added none, because the Gowans lead figure lots are not the same item.
lots.key_photo_findings: Crop of the box logo reads MADE BY THE ... PMC inside a diamond, next to MADE IN ENGLAND. The box art shows four horses and a seated driver. The contents show only two horses and no driver, although the lot title says DRIVER & HORSES. The cloth tilt is present. Paint on the horses looks mostly intact. The wheels are bright yellow.
lots.condition: The box is worn and grubby, with torn corners, a missing or split corner on the lid, creases and a small hole in the lid. The contents look fair to good and are packed in tissue. The driver may be missing (or hidden under the tilt or tissue), and the box art suggests a 4-horse team.
lots.question_for_gowans: Is there a driver figure in the box (the title says there is, but none shows in the photo), and how many horses are there? Is there any maker name on the base of the wagon or the horses? Is any paint lost or any part broken?
